newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's VSM to sell $150 mln of bonds to Indosuez.
newsitem.headline: Russia's VSM to sell $150 mln of bonds to Indosuez.

text.p: Russia's RAO Vysokoskorostnye Magistrali (VSM, or High-Speed Railways) will issue bonds worth $150 million and sell them to a group of banks headed by Bank Indosuez, a company official said on Monday.
VSM will make three rouble-denominated bond issues in 1997 and 1998, Deputy Financial Department Head Andrei Nikandrov told Reuters.
"We have already received confirmations from a banking group headed by Indosuez on their readiness to buy three VSM issues, each equalling $50 million, for roubles," Nikandrov said.
He said VSM would make two issues in 1997 and one issue in 1998.
VSM has aleady issued 510 billion roubles ($88.45 million) worth of one-year bonds to raise funds to build a high-speed rail link between Moscow and St Petersburg.
The government-backed bonds are the only corporate paper currently traded.
Nikandrov said the new issues would have a maturity of two years.
He also said that after the bank group had bought the paper, they were likely to be converted into securities similar to depositary receipts.
The Russian government guarantees $1.7 billion of VSM bond issues.
